title: Add Two Numbers Represented as a Linked List - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given two non-negative integers represented as linked lists with heads head1 and head2, where each node contains a single digit, return a new linked list representing their sum.

Note: The input lists may contain leading zeros, but the resulting sum list must not contain any leading zeros.

Examples:

Input: 


Explanation: Sum of 123 and 999 is 1122.

Input: 

Output: 7 -> 0
Explanation: Sum of 63 and 7 is 70.

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • Create a New Linked List - O(m + n) Time and O(max(m, n)) Space
  • Recursion - O(m + n) Time and O(max(m, n)) Space
  • Reuse the Longer List - O(m + n) Time and O(1) Auxiliary Space

Create a New Linked List - O(m + n) Time and O(max(m, n)) Space

Reverse both linked lists to add digits from right to left, and store the sum in a new linked list.

  • Reverse both linked lists to start adding from the least significant digit.
  • Create an empty result list and initialize carry = 0.
  • Traverse both lists, calculating sum = digit1 + digit2 + carry. If a list is exhausted, use 0 for its digit.cop
  • Create a new node with sum % 10 and update carry = sum / 10.
  • Append each new node to the result list.
  • If a carry remains, append a node for it.
  • Reverse the result list and remove leading zeros.
C++ 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Node {
  public:
    int data;
    Node *next;
    Node(int val) {
        data = val;
        next = nullptr;
    }
};

// Function to reverse the linked list
Node *reverse(Node *head) {
    Node *prev = nullptr, *curr = head, *next;

    while (curr != nullptr) {
        next = curr->next;
        curr->next = prev;
        prev = curr;
        curr = next;
    }
    return prev;
}

// Function to trim leading zeros in linked list
Node *trimLeadingZeros(Node* head) {
	while(head->next != nullptr && head->data == 0)
    	head = head->next;
	return head;
}

// Function to add two numbers represented by linked list
Node *addTwoLists(Node *num1, Node *num2) {
    Node *res = nullptr, *curr = nullptr;
    int carry = 0;

	num1 = trimLeadingZeros(num1);
	num2 = trimLeadingZeros(num2);
  
    num1 = reverse(num1);
    num2 = reverse(num2);

    // Iterate till either num1 is not empty or num2 is
    // not empty or carry is greater than 0
    while (num1 != nullptr || num2 != nullptr || carry != 0) {
        int sum = carry;

        if (num1 != nullptr) {
            sum += num1->data;
            num1 = num1->next;
        }

        if (num2 != nullptr) {
            sum += num2->data;
            num2 = num2->next;
        }
      
        Node* newNode = new Node(sum % 10);

        carry = sum / 10;

      	// If this is the first node, then make this node
      	// as the head of the resultant linked list
      	if(res == nullptr) {
        	res = newNode;
          	curr = newNode;
        }
      	else {
          	
          	// Append new node to resultant linked list
          	// and move to the next node
        	curr->next = newNode;
        	curr = curr->next;
        }
    }

    return reverse(res);
}
void printList(Node* head) {
    while (head != nullptr) {
        cout << head->data;
        if (head->next != nullptr)
            cout << " -> ";
        head = head->next;
    }
    cout << '\n';
}
int main() {

    Node *head1 = new Node(1);
    head1->next = new Node(2);
    head1->next->next = new Node(3);

    Node *head2 = new Node(9);
    head2->next = new Node(9);
    head2->next->next = new Node(9);

    Node* result = addTwoLists(head1, head2);
    printList(result);

    return 0;
}

Recursion - O(m + n) Time and O(max(m, n)) Space

This approach adds two linked lists without reversing them.

  • Pad the shorter list with leading zeros to make both lists equal in length.
  • Recursively reach the end of both lists and add corresponding digits while backtracking.
  • Create new nodes to store the sum and link them to form the result list.
  • If a carry remains after recursion, add a new node at the beginning of the result.

Consider the input:

Step 1: Pad num2 with two leading zeros to make both lists equal in length.

  • num1 = 0 -> 0 -> 6 -> 3
  • num2 = 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 7

Step 2: Recursion reaches the end of both lists, then adds corresponding digits while returning.

  • 3 + 7 + 0 = 10: Store 0, carry 1.
  • 6 + 0 + 1 = 7: Store 7, carry 0.
  • 0 + 0 + 0 = 0: Store 0, carry 0.
  • 0 + 0 + 0 = 0: Store 0, carry 0.

The result list is 0 -> 0 -> 7 -> 0.

Step 3: Remove the leading zeros from the result list.

Output: 7 -> 0

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Node
{
  public:
    int data;
    Node *next;
    Node(int val)
    {
        data = val;
        next = nullptr;
    }
};

// Function to get length of linked list
int getLength(Node *head)
{
    int len = 0;
    while (head)
    {
        len++;
        head = head->next;
    }
    return len;
}

// Function to trim leading zeros in linked list
Node *trimLeadingZeros(Node* head) {
	while(head->next != nullptr && head->data == 0)
    	head = head->next;
	return head;
}

// Function to pad shorter list with zeros at front
Node *padList(Node *head, int diff)
{
    while (diff--)
    {
        Node *newNode = new Node(0);
        newNode->next = head;
        head = newNode;
    }
    return head;
}

// Recursive function to add lists
Node *addListRec(Node *num1, Node *num2, int &carry)
{

    if (num1 == nullptr && num2 == nullptr)
        return nullptr;

    // Recurse to the end
    Node *nextNode = addListRec(num1->next, num2->next, carry);

    int sum = num1->data + num2->data + carry;

    Node *curr = new Node(sum % 10);
    carry = sum / 10;

    curr->next = nextNode;

    return curr;
}

// Main function to add two lists
Node *addTwoLists(Node *num1, Node *num2)
{

    int len1 = getLength(num1);
    int len2 = getLength(num2);

    // Pad shorter list
    if (len1 < len2)
        num1 = padList(num1, len2 - len1);
    else
        num2 = padList(num2, len1 - len2);

    int carry = 0;
    Node *result = addListRec(num1, num2, carry);

    // If carry remains, add new node at front
    if (carry)
    {
        Node *newNode = new Node(carry);
        newNode->next = result;
        result = newNode;
    }

    return trimLeadingZeros(result);
}

// Print the linked list
void printList(Node* head) {
    while (head != nullptr) {
        cout << head->data;
        if (head->next != nullptr)
            cout << " -> ";
        head = head->next;
    }
    cout << '\n';
}

Reuse the Longer List - O(m + n) Time and O(1) Auxiliary Space

Reuse the nodes of the longer linked list to store the sum instead of creating a separate result list.

Since the sum can have at most one more digit than the longer number, at most one extra node is needed to store a final carry.

  • Remove leading zeros from both linked lists.
  • Find the longer list, which will store the result.
  • Reverse both lists to start addition from the least significant digit.
  • Add corresponding digits along with the carry. Store the last digit of each sum in the corresponding node of the longer list and update the carry.
  • If the shorter list ends first, continue adding the remaining digits of the longer list along with the carry.
  • If a carry remains after all digits are processed, create one extra node to store it.
  • Reverse the modified longer list to restore the correct digit order and return it.

Consider the input:

Step 1: After removing the leading zeros, the lists become:

  • head1 = 6 -> 3 (represents 63)
  • head2 = 7 (represents 7)

Step 2: Identify the longer list

  • The first list has 2 nodes, while the second list has 1 node.
  • Therefore, the first list is used to store the result.

Step 3: Reverse both lists

  • head1 = 3 -> 6
  • head2 = 7

Step 4: Add corresponding digits

  • Add 3 + 7 + 0 = 10. Store 0 in the first node and set carry = 1.
  • Add 6 + 1 = 7. Store 7 in the second node and set carry = 0.

The reversed result is 0 -> 7.

Step 5: Restore the digit order

  • Reverse the result to obtain 7 -> 0.
  • No leading zeros need to be removed.

Output: 7 -> 0
